How to search, inspect and compare the records

Use the Evidence hub to find a claim, indicator, visual or source-backed record, then inspect the definition, group covered, calculation base, period, geography, method, limitations, source and evidence date. Compare records when similar labels may hide different units or populations. Disagreement, series breaks and missing evidence remain visible rather than being averaged or filled in. The hub is an index for verification; detailed evidence lives in the linked records and comparison view.

The official 2026 exchange and remittance roster can be counted; whether providers operate now is a separate question

The official 2026 roster of exchange and remittance providers issued by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) lists 98 exchange companies, 225 individual exchange establishments and 106 remittance agents. These are roster entries counted by the roster's own classes: the three class totals are not a count of unique providers, nor a verified count of providers operating now. Because the roster does not state its issue date, CBY-Aden's 2026 decisions (dated January to September 2026) suspending or withdrawing the licences of named entities, or closing their premises, are matched with the roster entity by entity, because a decision may or may not already be reflected in it.

Does not establish: Adding the three classes does not give a count of unique providers, because no rule for identifying the same entity across classes has been applied. Inclusion in the annual roster is not proof of current operation, branch activity or service availability, including for entities named in 2026 enforcement decisions.
Open evidence record →
Reference CLM-009

Evidence freshness differs by domain

The evidence here is not equally current across domains: several payments/regulatory observations are from 2025–2026, while key representative people-side evidence is older.

Does not establish: Older evidence is not invalid because of its age, and recent administrative evidence does not measure current financial inclusion across the population.
Open evidence record →
Reference CLM-014

Enforcement decisions are events, not a market census

Governor's decisions of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) dated January to September 2026 record licence withdrawals, suspensions and closures for specific exchange and remittance providers. This record covers selected CBY-Aden Governor's decisions of 2026 concerning exchange and remittance providers (Nos. 1–6, 9–11, 13–15, 17 and 18); other decision numbers are not included and their subjects are not assessed. The official 2026 roster can be counted by class, but these decisions are matched with it entity by entity and are not subtracted from it to produce a count of providers operating now.

Does not establish: The 2026 annual roster can be counted by class, but it is not a census of operating providers. Subtracting suspension, withdrawal and closure decisions from the roster does not give a current count of operating providers: the roster does not state its issue date, so each decision is matched to named entities one by one, without assuming whether the roster already reflects it. A provider not named in these decisions is not thereby shown to be active or compliant. The record does not cover 2026 decision numbers other than those listed, and it does not assess their subjects.
Open evidence record →
Reference CLM-019

Raw case shares are not population estimates

World Bank variable pages expose raw sample case counts and percentages for the Yemen Findex file, but explicitly warn that those figures cannot be interpreted as summary statistics of the population of interest.

Does not establish: The raw, unweighted case percentages shown on the World Bank variable pages are not estimates for Yemen's adult population and are not reported in this resource.
Open evidence record →
Reference CLM-024

There is no single latest year for all people-side evidence

The people-side evidence here does not have one latest year: account ownership has a latest verified Yemen aggregate in 2022, while weighted public evidence currently available here for account use, saving, borrowing and domestic-remittance behaviour is centered on 2014; latest-wave resilience and barrier values remain unpublished until the required weighted computation is complete. Historical results stay separate from any newer estimate until that computation and its verification are complete.

Does not establish: The 2014 behaviour values do not describe current behaviour, and raw case percentages from the 2021 wave are not a substitute for weighted population estimates.
Open evidence record →
Reference CLM-031

A public interface is not the same thing as the underlying dataset

World Bank public remittance interfaces do not expose Yemen history uniformly. One interface, reviewed on 10 September 2026, showed an older span of years, while other World Bank interfaces and earlier documented retrievals contained later observations. The difference reflects what each interface displays and how its data can be traced; it is not evidence that later underlying data are absent.

Does not establish: The difference does not show that data were deleted or withdrawn, or why any correction was made, and one public interface's observations are not a substitute for another's.
Open evidence record →
Reference CLM-039

IMF Staff-Monitored Program (SMP) for Yemen: staff-level agreement of July 2026, subject to Management approval

On 16 July 2026, staff of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the Yemeni authorities announced staff-level agreement on key policies and reforms that could underpin a proposed 18-month Staff-Monitored Program (SMP). The IMF stated that the agreement was subject to Management approval and would not result in Board discussion. It is not an IMF financing arrangement.

Does not establish: The proposed Staff-Monitored Program (SMP) is not an arrangement approved or endorsed by the Executive Board of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and does not involve IMF financing; the agreement is also not evidence that external-sector statistics have been reconciled.
Open evidence record →
Reference CLM-049

June and end-2023 borrower points are not one continuous series

The roughly 80,800 active-borrower point cited for June 2023 and the 78,686 end-2023 point come through different source chains. They are kept as separate observations until the provider sets and methods behind them are reconciled, and no June-to-year-end decline is calculated from them.

Does not establish: The two figures do not establish a decline between June and the end of 2023, monthly values between them, or a continuous series, while the provider sets behind them remain unreconciled.
Open evidence record →
Reference CLM-057

The SMEPS financial-services KPI is a programme result, not a national MSME rate

SMEPS's 2024 Annual Report reports that 19% of supported MSMEs accessed financial services in 2024, while the 2021–2024 total reported as achieved is 15% against a 40% programme target. The table does not fully specify the metric-specific assessment base or operational definition of 'accessed financial services'. The KPI can therefore be read only within the programme, subject to that limitation; it is not a national MSME access rate.

Does not establish: The percentage is not a national rate of access to financial services for micro, small and medium enterprises, a representative survey estimate or a national rate of unique firms, and it does not show that SMEPS caused access.
Open evidence record →
Reference CLM-060

Formal firms in the 2022 survey: accounts were common, bank finance for working capital was not

Among formal firms in the 2022 seven-governorate survey, 58.2% (191 of 328) reported a checking or savings account. Their working capital came mainly from internal sources: on average, 69.12% came from internal funds or retained earnings, 16.66% from money lenders, friends or relatives, 10.15% from advance payments by clients, 1.97% from non-bank financial institutions, 1.31% from supplier credit and 0.56% from banks. In a separate question on the financial intermediaries they use, 73.48% of responding formal firms named an exchange store or money exchanger and 24.39% a commercial bank; firms could name more than one, so these are not market shares. The evidence base does not record the number of firms behind the working-capital averages or the intermediary question. Among the 217 informal firms surveyed, 80.18% had no bank account; that sample was drawn from activity and location lists rather than a national register. The formal-firm sample includes micro firms with fewer than five employees, and neither sample represents all Yemeni firms.

Does not establish: The evidence base does not record the number of firms behind the working-capital averages or the intermediary question. An average working-capital share is not a share of firms, and multiple-response percentages are not market shares. Holding an account does not show that a firm uses bank credit. The formal and informal samples use different frames, so they cannot be added together or compared with the 2013 survey. Firms are not people, so these shares are not comparable with the Findex account-ownership rate.
Open evidence record →
Reference CLM-062

Where is the evidence current — and where is it old?

Evidence dates differ by domain: several payments and regulatory observations date from 2025–2026, while key representative evidence about people is older. Each item is placed by its observation or publication date and by its evidence type: representative survey, administrative record, regulatory material, secondary evidence or unresolved gap. Newer administrative data are not automatically a current population outcome, and older evidence is not automatically invalid.

Old evidence is not automatically invalid; recent administrative/regulatory evidence is not a current population outcome.

Reference VIS-MECHANISM-METRIC-BRIDGE

Consumer protection and complaint path: official rules and guidance

Evidence on the consumer-protection and complaint path of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden): the announcement of the 2023 Financial Consumer Protection Regulatory Instructions (28 August 2023), whose legal text has not been extracted here, and 2024 awareness material and a brochure describing the complaint and escalation steps. Actual complaint handling and redress outcomes are separate questions on which the evidence base holds no evidence.

The existence of a complaint and redress framework does not establish that consumers use it, that cases are resolved on time, or that redress outcomes are effective.
Open evidence record →
Reference DS-FCP-ARCH

Qualitative evidence register

A structured register of 20 reconciled qualitative evidence items used to interpret mechanisms, institutional conditions and source-specific narratives without turning them into population prevalence or causal estimates.

Qualitative evidence can support mechanisms and context, but it does not by itself establish population prevalence, quantified effect size or causality.
Open evidence record →
Reference DS-QUAL-EVIDENCE

OECD: institutional fragility and weak formal access (qualitative interpretation)

The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) links fragmented institutions, supervisory gaps and weak formal access to financial-sector fragility and low trust. The evidence is contextual interpretation, not measured prevalence or a causal effect estimate.

It cannot establish prevalence, a quantified level of trust or a causal effect size.
Open evidence record →
Reference QUAL-001

How many respondents answered each Findex question

Weighted estimates for the 2021 wave have not yet been produced, so no values are shown. When they are published, each will be accompanied by the number of respondents who gave a valid answer, the number of missing or invalid answers, and a note where a question was asked only of a sub-group; these counts describe the sample and are not population estimates.

Raw case percentages are not population prevalence rates, and indicators are not ranked by them.
Open evidence record →
Reference VIS-FINDEX-SAMPLE-SUPPORT

Latest observation for each people-side financial function

The latest weighted evidence differs by financial function: account ownership has a value from the 2021 Findex wave (11.9%, reported for 2022), while the latest weighted values for saving, borrowing and domestic remittances date from 2014 (20.6% of adults saved any money, 65.9% borrowed any money and 18.3% received domestic remittances), and weighted estimates of resilience and of the reasons for not having an account have not yet been calculated for the 2021 wave.

It is not a composite inclusion score. There is no single latest year for people-side evidence, and a recent date for one function does not make the evidence for another function current.
Open evidence record →
Reference VIS-DEMAND-VINTAGE-LADDER

Published historical Findex results for Yemen

Weighted Findex values for Yemen from the 2011 and 2014 waves, one value per measure and wave, each with its population base, missing values and publication status, so older measures stay interpretable without being presented as current.

Historical weighted values hold for their stated wave and base, but they do not establish current 2026 behaviour and do not describe later years unless newer comparable evidence is published.
Open evidence record →
Reference DS-FINDEX-PUBLIC-HISTORY

How recent the people-side evidence is, by financial function

Shows, for ten financial functions, the period that each function's evidence refers to, so that the people-side answer does not imply one common latest year.

The currentness map does not make older evidence current, and a function with no newer numeric observation remains an evidence gap rather than zero or an interpolated value.

Reference DS-DEMAND-VINTAGE-LENS

What kind of evidence is this?

Evidence in this resource falls into distinct types: weighted population measures, administrative records, perception studies, official secondary analysis, recommendations, and the stage a reform or programme has reached. Each type supports different conclusions; the types are not a ranking of truth or a numeric confidence score.

One type of evidence does not stand in for another: a perception is not a population outcome, a recommendation is not implementation, a project milestone is not usage, and an account or transaction is not a unique person. An evidence type is not a probability or certainty score, and the order in which types are presented does not rank them.
Open evidence record →
Reference VIS-EVIDENCE-CLASS-LADDER

Related measurement priorities

Consumer experience and redress outcomes

Official material specifies complaint and escalation architecture, including source-defined time windows; actual complaint volumes, resolution times and outcomes are not documented in the available evidence.

Evidence needed: Complaint and redress data from providers and the regulator, plus consumer-side evidence on experience, including fees, disclosure and trust.
